problem:
An object of mass $25\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the object is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=5\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts opposite to the direction of motion.

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the object? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the object are the weight due to gravity and drag.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$

feedback.problem:
A bag of cement of mass $30\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the bag is proportional to the square of its velocity and acts in the opposite direction to the direction of motion.
At a particular moment during the fall, the bag's velocity is $10\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $\frac{49}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the bag? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the body are the weight due to gravity and drag. 

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Terminal velocity is the constant speed a falling object approaches as the upward resistive force (drag) grows to exactly balance the downward gravitational force.
That is, at terminal velocity (a constant), acceleration is zero, so by $F=ma,$ the resultant force is zero.

First, note that only two forces act on the bag: the force due to gravity, given by the weight

$$
w=mg=30\cdot 9.8=294\,\text{N},
$$

and the force due to drag $D,$ which is proportional to the square of the velocity (and negative since it acts in the negative direction),

$$
D=-k{v}^{2},
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality. Hence, the resultant force acting on the body is

$$
F=w+D=294-k{v}^{2}.
$$

Applying Newton's second law, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\ 294-k{v}^{2} & =30a\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that, at a particular moment, the bag's velocity is $10\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $\frac{49}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ Substituting these values into the above, we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}294-k\cdot {(10)}^{2} & =30\cdot \frac{49}{9} \\ 294-100k & =\frac{1470}{9} \\ -100k & =-\frac{390}{3} \\ k & =\frac{392}{300} \\ k & =\frac{98}{75}\,\text{kg/m}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the resultant force acting on the bag is

$$
F=294-\frac{98}{75}{v}^{2}.
$$

When the bag reaches terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}},$ the resultant force is zero:

$$
294-\frac{98}{75}({v}_{\text{term}})^{2}=0\,⟹\,{v}_{\text{term}}=\sqrt{225}=15
$$

Therefore, the terminal velocity of the bag is ${v}_{\text{term}}=15\,\text{m/s}.$
